Any resume submitted outside of an active job posting will not be considered for employment.
*****INTERNS AND SEASONAL INTERNS ARE ELIGIBLE ONLY FOR PAID SICK LEAVE ACCRUED BASED ON HOURS WORKED. NO OTHER BENEFIT INCLUDING TECHNOLOGY STIPEND APPLY TO INTERNS OR SEASONAL INTERNS*****
Location: Chicago
Internship type: Year-round intern (1,000 hours max, January 2027–December 2027)
Hybrid Work Program
OCC operates under a Hybrid Work Program which, absent an approved exception, requires employees to work from an OCC office at least 3 days per week. To maximize in–person collaboration, Tuesday and Wednesday are considered anchor days, and all employees are expected to work in the office both days. Employees meeting performance expectations are generally permitted to select 2 other days per week to work remotely if desired. When working remotely, employees are generally expected to work from the state in which they reside, absent an exception approved by Human Resources. Additionally, OCC generally does not permit employees to work while traveling internationally.
About OCC:
A World Class Clearing Organization
The Options Clearing Corporation (OCC) is the world's largest equity derivatives clearing organization. Founded in 1973, OCC is dedicated to promoting stability and market integrity by delivering clearing and settlement services for options, futures and securities lending transactions. As a Systemically Important Financial Market Utility (SIFMU), OCC operates under the jurisdiction of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. OCC has more than 100 clearing members and provides central counterparty (CCP) clearing and settlement services to 21 exchanges and trading platforms.
OCC also provides free and engaging educational resources about the benefits and risks of options through its Options Industry Council (OIC).
OCC is building a culture that empowers continued learning, authentic innovation, and constant creativity.
About the Intern Program:
OCC is looking for interns who are eager to learn, humble enough to ask questions, and ready to think critically about complex problems. The OCC Internship Program equips students with the real-world skills needed to transition successfully into a career in financial services. As an intern, you will contribute to meaningful projects, applying your skills and knowledge to real challenges facing the business. Your time with us is a real opportunity to make a genuine impact on the future of OCC!
OCC's Year-Round Internship Program is a 12-month opportunity running from January through December and is open to both undergraduate and graduate students who are actively enrolled at a college or university. Interns work up to 20 hours per week during the school year and up to 40 hours per week during the summer, subject to a 1,000-hour cap. The role is based in a hybrid work environment, and overtime is not permitted.
About the Team & Role
Artificial Intelligence Research & Engineering (AIRE) is responsible for enterprise AI solution implementation and governance across OCC. AIRE evaluates emerging AI capabilities, builds secure and compliant platforms, and partners with business and technology teams to deliver AI-driven solutions that improve operational efficiency and decision-making. Core functions span Generative AI Solutions & Engineering, AI Governance & Risk Management, AI Vendor & Platform Management, and AI Training & Enablement.
Currently moving aggressively into agentic AI, leveraging frontier technologies, such as Anthropic's Claude platform and models, to transform how OCC operates, one functional area at a time.
This intern will work directly with our engineering team to help design, prototype, and evaluate agentic AI solutions built on frontier platforms. Depending on interests and skill set, contributions could include building and testing AI agent workflows, supporting governance and risk-review processes for new AI use cases, or helping assess vendor/platform capabilities. The intern will gain hands-on exposure to how a leading financial market infrastructure company is operationalizing generative and agentic AI at enterprise scale.
Job Summary & Responsibilities
This intern will join the AI Research & Engineering (AIRE) team and work hands-on building agentic AI solutions using frontier platforms (e.g., Anthropic's Claude models and tooling) to automate and enhance functional areas across OCC.
Projects & responsibilities may include:
Agent design & prototyping — Build and iterate on AI agent workflows for a specific OCC functional area, working alongside engineers who own these systems in production.
Platform integration — Integrate agentic solutions with internal data sources and APIs, gaining experience with the same MCP/tool-use patterns our engineers use to connect models to enterprise systems.
Evaluation & testing — Design test cases and evaluation frameworks to measure agent accuracy, reliability, and safety, which is a core ongoing responsibility for AI engineers ensuring solutions are production-ready.
Governance & risk awareness — Partner with the AI Governance & Risk Management functions to understand compliance and risk considerations for deploying AI in a regulated financial environment, a responsibility every AI engineer on the team shares.
Documentation & knowledge sharing — Document agent architectures, prompt designs, and lessons learned, contributing to the team's internal playbooks, mirroring how full-time engineers formalize and scale successful pilots.
Cross-functional collaboration — Work directly with business stakeholders in the target functional area to gather requirements and validate that the agentic solution solves a real operational problem, the same stakeholder-facing skill required in the full-time role.
Candidate Qualifications
Rising senior or second-year graduate student, graduating December 2027 or May/August 2028.
Desired Majors
Computer Science
Data Science
Statistics
Applied Mathematics / Mathematics
Engineering
Physics
Machine Learning
Financial Engineering / Financial Mathematics
Economics
Technical Skills/Experience Desired
We're looking for candidates with a strong quantitative/technical foundation and genuine curiosity about AI. Preferred skills are:
Solid programming skills in Python (most common) and/or SQL, Java, C++, or R
Coursework or project experience in machine learning, AI, or data science
Exposure to AI/ML frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Scikit-learn
Interest or experience in generative AI — LLMs, prompt engineering, or agentic systems
Familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP)
Experience with data pipelines or data engineering tools (Spark, Databricks, etc.)
Strong analytical thinking and ability to communicate technical work clearly
Curiosity, initiative (independent projects, research, hackathons), and a strong foundation for quick learning
Additional Qualifications
Strong academic performance (GPA 3.5+ preferred), reflecting rigor and consistency
Demonstrated initiative — independent projects, research, hackathons, or startup experience beyond coursework
Prior internship or work experience in a technical or analytical role preferred
Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Comfort working cross-functionally with business, risk, and technology teams
Strong problem-solving skills and a self-directed approach to learning new tools/technologies
Interest in financial services, market infrastructure, or regulated industries a plus
Familiarity with Agile/collaborative development practices (version control, code reviews, sprint-based work)

We are an integrated group of experts, industry leaders, academics, data scientists, and economists, working beyond borders and disciplines. We harness our collective expertise to deliver the inspired insights and practical strategies our clients need to stay ahead of what’s next.
About the Role
The work of a Summer Associate can have quantitative and qualitative aspects, depending on the needs of specific projects and the Summer Associate’s skills and interests. Projects range from subject matter research to data collection, to the preparation of economic, statistical, financial, and other forms of analysis. You will build technical skills and contribute to work that shapes important legal and business outcomes.
The Summer Associate program will be approximately 8 weeks long and begin in Summer 2027. We’re committed to helping our Summer Associates succeed by providing them with dedicated mentors, training programs, hands-on learning opportunities and support from industry experts. Our Summer Associate program is a pipeline program, and we aim to convert Summer Associates to full-time Associates after graduation, assuming the role is a fit on both ends.
What You’ll Do
Develop a practical understanding of industries, markets, legal claims, and business issues relevant to each engagement by gathering and reviewing information from our clients and their business, academic literature, legal documents, specialized industry resources, commercial databases, or other sources appropriate for the unique requirements of a project.
Identify, collect, develop, maintain, analyze and review data, qualitative materials, spreadsheets and other files as dictated by complex project needs.
Combine programming, model building, and statistical analysis skills using relational database and statistical programs to analyze a variety of subjects with software such as SQL, R, Stata, SAS, Python, or Snowflake.
Interact with senior staff, experts, and clients to clearly communicate questions, findings, economic and business concepts, and recommendations.
Demonstrate creativity and efficient analytical skills to develop novel solutions tailored to unique projects.
Provide valuable contributions to client deliverables and expert reports.
Qualifications
Progression towards a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Economics, Mathematics, Data Science, Statistics, Accounting, Business, Finance, Healthcare Administration or a related analytical field, with an expected graduation date between Winter 2027 and Summer 2028.
3.6 GPA or higher preferred.
Demonstrated interest in applying analytics to business, financial, legal, regulatory, or policy questions.
Strong quantitative, research, problem-solving, and written communication skills. 
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, client-service environment. 
Attention to detail, intellectual curiosity, and a commitment to producing high-quality work. 
Experience with statistical, econometric and programming tools such as Excel, Stata, R, Python, SQL or similar platforms is preferred.
Fluency with AI tools is desirable.
Candidates must be able to submit verification of their legal right to work in the United States, without company sponsorship now or in the future.  
Our Practice Areas
Summer Associates are hired to support project work aligned to one of BRG’s practice areas, though there may be flexibility to work across multiple practice areas. Candidates can select a preferred practice area as part of the application process. You can find more information about them below.
1. Antitrust & Competition: Experts in our antitrust practice apply learning from industrial organization, econometrics and microeconomic theory to provide testimony to counsel, corporations, and governments in matters involving antitrust litigation and merger reviews. Our experts and academic affiliates have testified in some of the largest and most significant antitrust matters of the past two decades, including antitrust actions involving platforms and multi-sided markets, automobile manufacturers, insurance companies, financial markets (e.g., LIBOR and foreign exchange) and other industries. Our project teams frequently evaluate industry conduct and assess antitrust liability, calculate damages from anticompetitive conduct and build simulation models to understand the impacts of proposed mergers.
2. Business Insurance Claims (BIC): We provide immediate and strategic guidance to policyholders following a catastrophe. Our BIC experts meticulously analyze financial data and operational records, develop robust financial models, and prepare comprehensive, well-documented insurance claims, accelerating resolution and maximizing claim payments.
3. Construction: We specialize in data analytics, litigation support, claims/dispute analysis, scheduling/logistics management and expert witness testimony within the construction, engineering, and architectural fields. Our team supports clients through budget and payment advisory, loss assessment and valuation, estimations and takeoffs, and insurance and damages claim valuations. We also specialize in providing our clients with budgetary and payment oversight, project management recommendations, project scheduling generation, and constructability and viability analyses for both upcoming and ongoing construction projects.
4. Commercial Disputes: We combine exceptional analytical and accounting skills and industry-specific knowledge to provide comprehensive support throughout the legal process. From initial case assessment and in-depth damages analysis to litigation support and expert testimony in hearings, trials, arbitration, regulatory proceedings, and mediation, we deliver data-driven insights to secure favorable outcomes.
5. Consumer Protection, Product Liability & Environment: Our experts are regularly engaged in matters involving claims of consumer fraud, product liability, false advertising, data privacy and data breach, and alleged violations of environmental and natural resource law. Associates in this area employ techniques from microeconomic theory, econometrics, marketing and environmental and resource economics to address in class certification, liability and damages.
6. Energy & Climate: We help clients across the global energy value chain address complex strategic, commercial, financial, market, regulatory, and dispute-related issues. Our work spans power and utilities, oil and gas, renewables, storage, advanced nuclear, eMobility, hydrogen and low-carbon fuels, carbon management, infrastructure, and the broader energy transition. We conduct rigorous market research, economic modeling, and detailed reporting, helping clients address legal and business challenges.
7. Financial Institutions Advisory: We are a trusted advisor to leading financial services companies. We work to help clients meet and execute strategies related to risk and regulation, compliance, financial crime, innovations in technology, accounting, cryptocurrency and blockchain, business process outsourcing, the Bank Secrecy Act, anti-money laundering, lookbacks, data quality, and evolving customer experience expectations.
8. Healthcare Advisory: As healthcare organizations navigate increasing reimbursement pressure, workforce challenges, regulatory and enforcement complexity, and rapid technological change, we work alongside executive teams and governing bodies to identify opportunities, implement practical solutions, and deliver measurable, lasting results. Our integrated team combines deep industry expertise across strategy, revenue management, operational excellence, clinical transformation, and technology and AI with the comprehensive capabilities of a global advisory firm and the agility, senior attention, and client service of a boutique consultancy.
9. Healthcare Analytics and Disputes: We tackle complex legal and operational challenges in the healthcare industry using data-driven, objective, and innovative approaches. Our experts lead advisory, risk management, and litigation matters, combining deep healthcare industry expertise with cutting edge research, analytics and financial modeling.
10. Intellectual Property: Our intellectual property experts and academic affiliates regularly testify on damages, trademark confusion, irreparable harm and commercial success. Many of our matters require expertise in consumer behavior, judgment and decision-making and our project teams work on some of the world's largest patent infringement, trademark infringement, trade secret misappropriation, and copyright infringement cases. Associates in this practice regularly build econometric models of market prices, analyze survey data and the results of choice experiments and assist with the preparation of expert reports and other client deliverables.
Locations
Summer Associates will primarily be hired in locations like Boston, Washington DC, Chicago, New York, Houston, Los Angeles and the San Francisco Bay Area. There are also a limited number of opportunities in smaller offices like Tampa and Pittsburgh. Summer Associates are expected to work in the office five days per week to take full advantage of the mentorship, collaboration, and relationship-building opportunities that support their professional growth. Remote roles for practices that require frequent travel to client sites are also available.

Atlas Tube, a division of Zekelman Industries, is seeking a highly motivated Supply Chain Intern to join our team for Summer 2027. Reporting directly to the Manager, Inventory and Replenishment, you will gain hands-on experience supporting inventory management, automated replenishment processes, supply planning, and data-driven decision-making within a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
Working closely with Supply Chain, Sales, IT, Operations, Customer Experience, and other cross-functional teams, you will support the organization's Automated Inventory Management (AIM) program through data analysis, reporting, process improvement, and inventory management activities. This internship offers an excellent opportunity to learn how technology, analytics, and supply chain strategy work together to support customer service and operational excellence.
The ideal candidate is analytical, detail-oriented, and eager to learn. This role is well suited for students interested in supply chain management, operations, business analytics, or manufacturing who want to develop real-world experience while contributing to meaningful projects.
What You'll Do
Assist with maintaining and updating customer, inventory, and replenishment data within the AIM program.
Help identify, investigate, and resolve data discrepancies, reporting issues, and system exceptions.
Collaborate with Supply Chain, IT, Sales, Operations, and Customer Experience teams to support inventory and replenishment processes.
Help develop reports, dashboards, presentations, and documentation to support business decisions.
Participate in process improvement initiatives focused on efficiency, data accuracy, and customer service.
Gather, analyze, and report on inventory consumption, replenishment activity, and AIM program performance metrics.
Review inventory trends and help evaluate supply planning recommendations to support inventory optimization.
Assist with monitoring replenishment processes to help ensure materials are available to meet customer demand.
Work with internal stakeholders to support ongoing inventory management and continuous improvement efforts.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Who You Are
Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Analytics, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
Strong analytical mindset with a passion for solving problems using data and process improvement.
Detail-oriented and capable of managing multiple priorities while maintaining accuracy.
Effective communicator who enjoys collaborating with cross-functional teams.
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
Comfortable analyzing data and translating findings into actionable insights.
Strong organizational, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
Experience with SAP, data analytics tools, EDI systems, or automation technologies is a plus.
Interest in pursuing a career in supply chain, inventory management, operations, or manufacturing.
